summary: Reselected a new sourced question after the read-index ack thread was explained: whether a MsgReadIndex postponed because the leader has not committed in its term is ever completed with a stale read index once the queued duty survives an authority transition. Traced admission (stepLeader queues without caching any index or term), survival (raft.reset does not clear pendingReadIndexMessages, so the queue outlives step-down, re-election and removal), and completion (release only from the leader's MsgAppResp path under current leadership, using the live r.raftLog.committed). Because every write to raftLog.committed is guarded to be non-decreasing (commitTo, the log-restore guard, and loadState), the completed index is at least the admission-time index. Recorded the queue lifecycle as a behavior, the monotonicity argument, and an explained negative that refutes the stale-index suspicion, with retained contract properties and explicit source-only limitations.
